text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.

-Communist East Germany let its spies take over the identities of children born under Hitler's Lebensborn programme to infiltrate Norway and other Western countries. The Norwegian intelligence has known since the 1970s about the scheme, which was revealed by German magazine Der Spiegel on Saturday.
-Six percent of women and 16 percent of men in Oslo are heavy drinkers. Women have more alcohol problems than they used to.
-Norway's first Hindu temple was inaugurated at the weekend in a former community centre in Oslo.
-Smedvig Offshore in Stavanger has taken home its drill rigs West Delta and West Vanguard in order for them to fly the Norwegian flag. They were previously registered in Liberia.
-Statoil has now distributed around 11,000 powerful Compaq Presario PC's to its staff in Norway, Sweden and Denmark for use at home.
-Scandinavia Online is dumping software prices charged to companies who want their own page on the Internet.
-Several opposition parties in parliament are demanding that the government grants metals maker Elkem lower electricity prices for its aluminium smelter in Sauda.
